item.annotation: El libro está de hecho compuesto de tres partes, unidas por cierta simpatía hispanista. Considera que América Latina no ha sido entendida porque se le han aplicado categorías extrañas o extranjerizantes, especialmente en el caso de la "metodología anglosajona". En otro aspecto del libro se intenta mostrar que el espíritu democrático latinoamericano proviene del pensamiento político español, incluyendo la Escuela de Salamanca en el siglo XVI. Todavía en otro se reconocen tres clases de humanismo en los siglos XVII y XVIII, culminando en un "humanismo ilustrado", que no debe confundirse con el "enciclopédico", el cual nunca habría arraigado en América. item.annotation: In this complex and thoughtful study, Bracamonte y Sosa examines two pillars of Maya philosophy: the cyclical nature of time, and prophesies or prognostications (vaticinios). The author explores the style and form of the cycles of time that specialists used to construct abstract ideas, and to foresee the future. Most impressively, the author attempts to trace the development of these two aspects of Maya culture across time, from prehispanic times to the early years of the 21st century. The book is organized accordingly, considering the long-term effect of modernity and Westernization on Mayan concepts of the world and cosmology.

item.annotation: This collection of essays explores the highly confusing "second phase" of the Mexican Revolution, from the February 1913 overthrow and assassination of President Francisco Madero to the reestablishment of the revolutionary government under north Mexico politician Venustiano Carranza. item.annotation: El libro está de hecho compuesto de tres partes, unidas por cierta simpatía hispanista. Considera que América Latina no ha sido entendida porque se le han aplicado categorías extrañas o extranjerizantes, especialmente en el caso de la "metodología anglosajona". En otro aspecto del libro se intenta mostrar que el espíritu democrático latinoamericano proviene del pensamiento político español, incluyendo la Escuela de Salamanca en el siglo XVI. Todavía en otro se reconocen tres clases de humanismo en los siglos XVII y XVIII, culminando en un "humanismo ilustrado", que no debe confundirse con el "enciclopédico", el cual nunca habría arraigado en América. item.annotation: In this complex and thoughtful study, Bracamonte y Sosa examines two pillars of Maya philosophy: the cyclical nature of time, and prophesies or prognostications (vaticinios). The author explores the style and form of the cycles of time that specialists used to construct abstract ideas, and to foresee the future. Most impressively, the author attempts to trace the development of these two aspects of Maya culture across time, from prehispanic times to the early years of the 21st century. The book is organized accordingly, considering the long-term effect of modernity and Westernization on Mayan concepts of the world and cosmology.

item.annotation: This collection of essays explores the highly confusing "second phase" of the Mexican Revolution, from the February 1913 overthrow and assassination of President Francisco Madero to the reestablishment of the revolutionary government under north Mexico politician Venustiano Carranza. Key issues include the weaknesses of the early Madero government; the often conflicting dynamics of political versus military revolutions; and the different legal and philosophical positions of the revolutionary factions. The essays of the latter half of the book tend toward legal and constitutional issues, and demonstrate considerable sympathy toward the often-criticized Carranza.

item.annotation: El libro está de hecho compuesto de tres partes, unidas por cierta simpatía hispanista. Considera que América Latina no ha sido entendida porque se le han aplicado categorías extrañas o extranjerizantes, especialmente en el caso de la "metodología anglosajona". En otro aspecto del libro se intenta mostrar que el espíritu democrático latinoamericano proviene del pensamiento político español, incluyendo la Escuela de Salamanca en el siglo XVI. Todavía en otro se reconocen tres clases de humanismo en los siglos XVII y XVIII, culminando en un "humanismo ilustrado", que no debe confundirse con el "enciclopédico", el cual nunca habría arraigado en América. item.annotation: In this complex and thoughtful study, Bracamonte y Sosa examines two pillars of Maya philosophy: the cyclical nature of time, and prophesies or prognostications (vaticinios). The author explores the style and form of the cycles of time that specialists used to construct abstract ideas, and to foresee the future. Most impressively, the author attempts to trace the development of these two aspects of Maya culture across time, from prehispanic times to the early years of the 21st century. The book is organized accordingly, considering the long-term effect of modernity and Westernization on Mayan concepts of the world and cosmology.

item.annotation: This collection of essays explores the highly confusing "second phase" of the Mexican Revolution, from the February 1913 overthrow and assassination of President Francisco Madero to the reestablishment of the revolutionary government under north Mexico politician Venustiano Carranza. Key issues include the weaknesses of the early Madero government; the often conflicting dynamics of political versus military revolutions; and the different legal and philosophical positions of the revolutionary factions. The essays of the latter half of the book tend toward legal and constitutional issues, and demonstrate considerable sympathy toward the often-criticized Carranza.
